executive_summary: Collection window February 15-21, 2028: New York Fashion Week Fall/Winter 2028 women's shows, which opened within the 2028-02-08 window, closed out within this window. Khaite's own site published the house's runway lookbook for its Fall/Winter 2028 New York show, and wwd.com independently reviewed the same show, both identifying a cantilevered-shoulder blazer -- a tailored blazer built with an internal structural framework that extends the shoulder line beyond the wearer's natural silhouette in a rigid, unsupported-looking projection -- as a recurring construction across multiple looks. This is treated as genuine cross-sector corroboration, applying the identical reasoning already used for the 2028-01-24 Louis Vuitton, 2028-01-31 Dior, and 2028-02-14 Proenza Schouler signals: one designer_origin source (the house's own lookbook) and one editorial source doing independent runway-review reporting, not a restatement of the house's own materials. Separately, the British Fashion Council published its official calendar for London Fashion Week Fall/Winter 2028, and vogue.com independently reported on the announcement with added confirmed-participant detail beyond a restatement of the BFC's own release -- the same fact pattern already applied to the 2028-02-07 CFDA/wwd.com New York calendar-confirmation signal and the 2028-01-10 FHCM/wwd.com Paris menswear calendar-confirmation signal. Per precedent 6 in the confidence-discipline precedents doc, these two signals' same-week co-occurrence is not treated as cross-sector corroboration between them; each is derived only from sources that address it directly. The Proenza Schouler spiral-seam-wrap-coat thread, the resort 2028 puffer-shell skirt thread, the resale-demand signal on structured waist-tailoring, the obi-sash cocoon coat thread, and the opera-glove/'restraint dressing' thread all produced no new development this window and are not carried forward again absent fresh movement. The Margiela raw-edge thread remains closed out as of 2027-10-18. Met Gala 2027, Wales Bonner, and CFDA's Fashion Fund/Awards remain untracked going forward per standing convention.

top_signals.name: Khaite Fall/Winter 2028 runway: cantilevered-shoulder blazer
top_signals.evidence: Khaite published its own runway lookbook for its Fall/Winter 2028 show at New York Fashion Week, and wwd.com independently reviewed the same show, both identifying a blazer built with an internal structural framework that extends the shoulder line past the wearer's natural silhouette in a rigid, unsupported-looking projection -- repeated across multiple looks. The lookbook is the house's own first-party statement of the collection; wwd.com's review adds independent critical framing rather than restating the lookbook's own copy.
top_signals.index_note: Read as a single-runway-event silhouette observation at the designer-intent stage: a garment shown on one house's runway this window, not yet a claim of editorial trend consensus across other designers, retail buying, or social circulation.

top_signals.name: London confirms Fall/Winter 2028 women's Fashion Week dates
top_signals.evidence: The British Fashion Council, London Fashion Week's governing body, published its official calendar for Fall/Winter 2028 women's London Fashion Week this window, the next leg of the international fashion-month sequence following New York's close. vogue.com independently reported on the announcement, adding a preliminary confirmed-designer-participant list not present in the BFC's own release -- this is treated as genuine independent second-sector reporting rather than a reprint of the primary announcement, the same distinction drawn for the 2028-02-07 nyfw-fw28-womens-calendar-confirmed signal and the 2028-01-10 pfw-mens-fw28-calendar-confirmed signal.
top_signals.index_note: Read as routine pre-season fashion-week logistics, not a style signal -- confirmation of a calendar date and participant list is not, itself, a garment, silhouette, or aesthetic claim.
top_signals.human_editor_note: derive_confidence() computes 'high' here (corroboration_count=2, two distinct sectors: institutional, editorial) and this report adopts that result rather than overriding it, applying the identical reasoning already used for the 2028-02-07 CFDA/wwd.com and 2028-01-10 FHCM/wwd.com calendar-confirmation signals: vogue.com's coverage adds confirmed-participant detail the BFC's own release did not include, which is genuine independent journalism, not a reprint of the primary announcement (contrast the 2027-09-06 fhcm.paris/laforma.club aggregator-reprint case under precedent 4). limitations: Two signals cleared this report's corroboration bar this window: a designer-intent silhouette observation (Khaite) and a fashion-week scheduling confirmation (London), both reaching 'high' on genuine cross-sector corroboration -- see each signal's human_editor_note.

The Khaite signal reflects designer intent observed on a single runway this window, reported through one first-party channel and one independent editorial review; it does not represent editorial-consensus interpretation across other houses, retail adoption, or social amplification, none of which have occurred yet within this window.
Per precedent 6 in the confidence-discipline precedents doc, the two signals' same-week co-occurrence is not treated as cross-sector corroboration between them.
